text:
Recent work supports separating semantic relatedness from recommendation usefulness. AgentDR (2026) explicitly reasons about substitutes and complements using user history; function-based complementary recommendation research (2025) develops more specific relationship annotations. Neither relationship alone establishes purchase intent or compatibility. Recommendation judge research (2025–2026) finds that richer metadata and longer histories improve human agreement, but item-level agreement remains moderate even when aggregate system rankings agree strongly. These findings support qualitative diagnostics alongside the pinned validation metric. Sources: [AgentDR](https://www.amazon.science/publications/agentdr-dynamic-recommendation-with-implicit-item-item-relations-via-llm-based-agents), [function-based labels](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167865525003976), [recommendation judge evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23312).

A practical adaptation is an evidence-linked rubric: immediate usefulness, broad relatedness, substitute/complement relationship, explicit prerequisite mismatch, likely duplicate, and lower-ranked specific match. Store supporting history IDs and title/description excerpts; label compatibility, ownership, or intent unknown whenever evidence is insufficient. Similar titles alone cannot establish an unwanted duplicate. Calibrate against available feedback from the twenty users, separating rubric development from assessment and reporting supported-label coverage, abstention, per-label agreement, and uncertainty clustered by user. Twenty users provide limited evidence for generalization. “Trust or Escalate” (ICLR 2025) formalizes calibrated selective judging, with guarantees conditional on its statistical assumptions—not raw judge confidence. As an experimental proposal, supported failures can motivate relation-aware sampling or pairwise losses; avoid treating unknown cases as negatives or suppressing substitutes universally. Accept changes only through macro validation HR@10, without inferring diversity or conformity traits. Source: [Trust or Escalate](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/08dabd5345b37fffcbe335bd578b15a0-Paper-Conference.pdf).
